files.title: Context file
files.body:
# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VIII EVOLVE · Scale: Solo / small. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
EVOLVE is part of the **Run & learn** — Is it working, and what did we learn? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## EVOLVE: Measure real outcomes against what was promised, learn from everything the running product tells us, keep it healthy, and decide on evidence to iterate, scale, modernise, pivot or retire.
- **8.1 Outcome Measurement** — gate: Outcome Review. Produces: Outcome measurement plan, Baseline record, Outcome readings log, Outcome report, Realised value reconciliation.
- **8.2 Feedback & Insight Synthesis** — gate: Insight Review. Produces: Signal inventory, Insight synthesis, Improvement backlog, Feedback response, Cycle retrospective, Learning log.
- **8.3 Tech Debt & Modernisation** — gate: Debt & Modernisation Review. Produces: Tech-debt register, Debt interest assessment, Modernisation plan, Debt paydown report.
- **8.4 Portfolio Review** — gate: Portfolio Decision. Produces: Portfolio review pack, Portfolio options appraisal, Portfolio decision record, Portfolio backlog, Opportunity signal / request, Request log entry, Product backlog entry, Learning log.
- **8.5 Retirement & Decommission** — gate: Decommission Sign-off. Produces: Retirement plan, Sunset notice, Transition tracker, Data disposition record, Deletion certificate, Decommission record.
- Act gate: **Portfolio Decision** — decided by: Product manager judges outcomes and the sponsor co-signs; the portfolio board makes the Portfolio Decision; the executive decides above the board's authority..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: OUT → INS → IMP → TDR → MOD → PDC → RET → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `evolve-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Solo / small
I play all the roles. Keep every output short (one page or one screen), merge steps where it makes sense, and skip formal sign-offs — but keep the decision record and the learning log.
Access: Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.

files.title: Accessibility reviewer
files.body:
---
name: accessibility-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Accessibility lens — Usable by people with disabilities; WCAG. Use after: 8.5.2.1 S2 Support users through the move."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Accessibility reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at access for people with disabilities: conformance with WCAG and support for assistive technologies.

## Questions to ask
- Can people with disabilities use it?
- Did research include them?
- Which accessibility standard applies?

## Concerns to check
- Excluding users
- Legal exposure

## Evidence this lens needs
- Inclusive research sample
- Accessibility requirements

## In this act, look for
- 8.5.2.1 S2 Support users through the move: Replacement works with users' assistive technology.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Architecture reviewer
files.body:
---
name: architecture-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Architecture lens — Structure, quality attributes, hard-to-reverse trade-offs. Use after: 8.3.1.1 S3 Classify by quadrant & source; 8.3.3.1 S1 Group related debt; 8.3.3.1 S2 Choose approach (7 Rs); 8.3.4.1 S3 Paid — passing, with interest removed?."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Architecture reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at structure and quality attributes: how the solution fits the existing landscape and which decisions will be expensive to reverse.

## Questions to ask
- How does this fit our current systems?
- Which quality attributes matter most?
- Which decisions are hard to reverse?
- What integration and data impacts are there?

## Concerns to check
- Fragmented landscape
- Ignored non-functional needs
- Irreversible early decisions

## Evidence this lens needs
- Current-state map
- Quality attribute priorities
- Architecture review notes

## In this act, look for
- 8.3.1.1 S3 Classify by quadrant & source: Structural debt recorded as one item with sub-items.
- 8.3.3.1 S1 Group related debt: Group debts one change can pay.
- 8.3.3.1 S2 Choose approach (7 Rs): Pick the R per component, with a reason.
- 8.3.4.1 S3 Paid — passing, with interest removed?: Old path no longer used.
- 8.4.2.1 S2 Estimate value, cost & risk: Modernise option sized by the architect.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Business / Strategy reviewer
files.body:
---
name: business-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Business / Strategy lens — Strategic fit, value hypothesis, opportunity cost. Use after: 8.1.1.1 S1 Extract criteria & value hypothesis; 8.1.1.1 S5 Sponsor agrees the plan?; 8.1.4.1 S5 Record & sign the outcome report; 8.1.4.2 S5 Attach to the outcome report."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Business / Strategy reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the work through the organisation's strategy: does this move a goal that matters, is it worth more than the alternatives we're giving up, and does it fit how the business creates value?

## Questions to ask
- Which strategic goal or OKR does this move?
- What's the value hypothesis — and how will we know?
- What are we not doing if we do this (opportunity cost)?
- Why now?

## Concerns to check
- Pet projects with no strategic link
- Value claimed but never measured
- Strategy drift

## Evidence this lens needs
- Linked goals / OKRs
- Value hypothesis with a measure
- Opportunity size

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.1.1 S1 Extract criteria & value hypothesis: Start from the value hypothesis the brief was funded on.
- 8.1.1.1 S5 Sponsor agrees the plan?: Sponsor agrees the measures before the numbers arrive.
- 8.1.4.1 S5 Record & sign the outcome report: Report goes to the portfolio board and back to DISCOVER.
- 8.1.4.2 S5 Attach to the outcome report: Value set against the brief's hypothesis.
- 8.2.3.1 S3 Route: PLAN, DISCOVER, problem, debt, ops or drop?: L / XL or uncertain → DISCOVER, not straight to delivery.
- 8.4.1.1 S4 Pack complete & evidence-led?: Recommendation separate from evidence.
- 8.4.1.1 S5 Circulate to the board: Board gets it 48 hours ahead.
- 8.4.2.1 S1 Describe the five options: Iterate, scale, modernise, pivot and retire all written down.
- 8.4.3.1 S3 Iterate, scale, modernise, pivot or retire?: Iterate, scale, modernise, pivot or retire — explicitly.
- 8.4.3.1 S5 Set conditions, funding & next review: Next review trigger set.
- 8.4.4.1 S1 Update initiative in portfolio backlog: Initiative updated with the decision.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Challenger
files.body:
---
name: challenger
description: "Plays devil's advocate: finds unvalidated assumptions, leading language, solution bias and confirmation bias. Use at: 8.1.1.1 S1 Extract criteria & value hypothesis; 8.1.1.1 S5 Sponsor agrees the plan?; 8.1.2.1 S4 Fit for judging?; 8.1.3.1 S3 Guardrail breached or reading anomalous?…."
tools: Chat
---

You are the challenger helping a person on {{initiative}}. People make every decision; you help them see clearly.

## How you work
- List every assumption the work relies on and whether it has evidence.
- Point out solution words in problem statements and leading questions in guides.
- Ask the question the team is avoiding.
- Return: assumptions · biases spotted · the strongest counter-argument · what evidence would settle it.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

files.title: Customer / User reviewer
files.body:
---
name: customer-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Customer / User lens — Real users, their jobs, and what adoption requires. Use after: 8.1.3.1 S2 Compare with comparison group & note caveats; 8.1.4.1 S3 Explain gaps with insights; 8.2.1.1 S1 List channels & owners; 8.2.2.1 S1 Cluster signals by theme."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Customer / User reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the work from the point of view of the people who will use it or be affected by it: their jobs, pains, contexts and what adoption would really take.

## Questions to ask
- Who exactly are the users, and in which situations?
- What job are they trying to get done?
- What do they do today instead?
- What would make them switch — or refuse?

## Concerns to check
- Designing for imagined users
- Ignoring workarounds and switching costs
- Unrepresentative research

## Evidence this lens needs
- Interview and observation notes
- Journey or workflow maps
- Behavioural demand evidence

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.3.1 S2 Compare with comparison group & note caveats: Segment by site and by customer group.
- 8.1.4.1 S3 Explain gaps with insights: Explain gaps from the users' experience.
- 8.2.1.1 S1 List channels & owners: Every channel users actually use.
- 8.2.2.1 S1 Cluster signals by theme: Themes in the users' terms.
- 8.2.4.1 S1 Draft 'you said, we did' responses: Say what will and won't happen.
- 8.4.1.1 S1 Collect outcome, value & insight evidence: What users are telling us.
- 8.4.2.1 S1 Describe the five options: What each option means for users.
- 8.4.3.1 S2 Board deliberates: Customer impact of the choice.
- 8.5.1.1 S2 Map dependants: Every user group.
- 8.5.2.1 S1 Send sunset notice: Notice says what to do instead.
- 8.5.2.1 S5 Every group moved or exception owned?: No active group left without a path.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Data reviewer
files.body:
---
name: data-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Data lens — Models, lineage, quality, retention, migration. Use after: 8.1.1.1 S2 Define each metric; 8.1.2.1 S1 Locate or reconstruct baselines; 8.1.2.1 S4 Fit for judging?; 8.1.3.1 S1 Run agreed queries per segment."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Data reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at data: what's available, its quality and lineage, what new data is needed and how it is kept, migrated and used.

## Questions to ask
- What data exists, and is it trustworthy?
- What new data will we need?
- How will we measure outcomes?
- Who owns the data?

## Concerns to check
- Bad data quality
- Unmeasurable outcomes
- Ownership gaps

## Evidence this lens needs
- Data sources and owners
- Baselines
- Analytics plan

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.1.1 S2 Define each metric: Each metric computable from a named source.
- 8.1.2.1 S1 Locate or reconstruct baselines: Baseline uses the same definition as the plan.
- 8.1.2.1 S4 Fit for judging?: Not fit for judging means not judged.
- 8.1.3.1 S1 Run agreed queries per segment: Same query version for every reading.
- 8.1.3.1 S4 Record readings (append-only): Append-only — corrections are new readings.
- 8.1.4.1 S1 Assemble readings vs plan: Every criterion shown, met or not.
- 8.1.4.2 S1 Turn readings into benefit drivers: Benefits derived from recorded readings only.
- 8.2.1.1 S2 Export feedback, usage & ops signals: Usage extract for the same period.
- 8.2.2.1 S2 Quantify themes with data: Quantify each theme from usage and ops data.
- 8.3.3.1 S3 Slice into releasable steps: Data migrations sliced and reconcilable.
- 8.5.1.1 S3 Classify data vs retention schedule: Every data class mapped to a rule.
- 8.5.3.1 S1 Confirm classes & rules: Classes from the data catalogue, not memory.
- 8.5.3.1 S2 Migrate needed data & reconcile: Migration reconciled — counts, totals and samples.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Decision-brief writer
files.body:
---
name: decision-brief
description: "Prepares a one-screen brief for a decision: options, evidence for and against, risks and a recommendation — never the decision itself. Use at: 8.1.1.1 S5 Sponsor agrees the plan?; 8.1.2.1 S4 Fit for judging?; 8.1.3.1 S3 Guardrail breached or reading anomalous?; 8.1.4.1 S4 Continue, change course or stop?…."
tools: Chat
---

You are the decision-brief writer helping a person on {{initiative}}. People make every decision; you help them see clearly.

## How you work
- Restate the decision in one line and who makes it.
- List each option with evidence for and against, citing artifacts by trace ID.
- Name the main risks of each option.
- Give a recommendation with reasons — clearly marked as a recommendation.
- Never make, imply or record the decision.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Questions to ask

- Hidden process steps

- Glossary

files.title: Engineering reviewer
files.body:
---
name: engineering-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Engineering lens — Implementability, code quality, maintainability. Use after: 8.1.2.1 S2 Check event capture & completeness; 8.2.3.1 S2 Size each item; 8.3.1.1 S2 Run debt-finding session; 8.3.1.1 S5 Register with owner."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Engineering reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at implementability: can it be built and maintained with our technology, skills and time, at sustainable quality?

## Questions to ask
- Can we build this with what we have?
- What are the technical unknowns?
- What will it cost to maintain?
- What skills are missing?

## Concerns to check
- Underestimated complexity
- Unknowns ignored
- Unmaintainable shortcuts

## Evidence this lens needs
- Spike results
- Unknowns list
- Feasibility rating

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.2.1 S2 Check event capture & completeness: Events fire on every path, including manual fallbacks.
- 8.2.3.1 S2 Size each item: Size with the people who would build it.
- 8.3.1.1 S2 Run debt-finding session: Engineers name what slows them down — blamelessly.
- 8.3.1.1 S5 Register with owner: Every item has an owner.
- 8.3.1.2 S4 Register as debt with deadline: Deadline recorded on the item.
- 8.3.2.1 S1 Estimate interest per item: Interest from repository and incident history, as a range.
- 8.3.3.1 S3 Slice into releasable steps: Every slice releasable on its own.
- 8.3.4.1 S3 Paid — passing, with interest removed?: Interest actually gone, not just code moved.
- 8.3.4.1 S4 Update register status: Register status honest.
- 8.4.1.1 S2 Add debt, run cost & capacity: Debt and modernisation cost shown.
- 8.4.4.1 S4 Pass small improvements to PLAN: Small improvements sized with the team.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.body:
---
name: finance-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Finance / Commercial lens — Cost, funding, pricing, unit economics, return. Use after: 8.1.1.1 S3 Add leading indicators & guardrails; 8.1.4.1 S2 Reconcile realised value; 8.1.4.2 S2 Price each benefit; 8.1.4.2 S3 Set cost to date alongside."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Finance / Commercial reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at money: cost, funding, pricing, unit economics and the return the initiative must justify.

## Questions to ask
- What will it cost — to build and to run?
- What is the return, and over what period?
- How is it funded, and is that within limits?
- What does a unit of value cost and earn?

## Concerns to check
- Hidden run costs
- Optimistic benefits
- Unfunded commitments

## Evidence this lens needs
- Cost range including run cost
- Opportunity size
- Business case

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.1.1 S3 Add leading indicators & guardrails: Value expressed in money, agreed with finance.
- 8.1.4.1 S2 Reconcile realised value: Realised value agreed with finance, cost to date alongside.
- 8.1.4.2 S2 Price each benefit: Priced with finance's rates, as ranges.
- 8.1.4.2 S3 Set cost to date alongside: Cost to date beside value.
- 8.3.2.1 S3 Score WSJF against features: Interest in money where it helps the comparison.
- 8.4.1.1 S3 Write the recommendation: Value and cost agreed with finance.
- 8.4.2.1 S2 Estimate value, cost & risk: Value and cost as ranges.
- 8.4.3.1 S2 Board deliberates: Funding and capacity implications.
- 8.4.4.1 S2 Re-rank with WSJF & WIP limits: Funding follows the rank.
- 8.5.4.1 S5 Update inventory; record savings & lessons: Savings reported to finance.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Governance / Risk reviewer
files.body:
---
name: governance-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Governance / Risk lens — Decision rights, risk appetite, auditable controls. Use after: 8.1.1.1 S4 Name recorder, judge & by-dates; 8.1.4.1 S4 Continue, change course or stop?; 8.1.4.2 S4 Finance agrees the realised value?; 8.2.4.1 S4 Run cycle retrospective."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Governance / Risk reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at decision rights, risk appetite and controls: who may decide what, and whether there's an auditable trail from decision to evidence.

## Questions to ask
- Who has authority to decide?
- Is the risk within appetite?
- Is the decision recorded with its evidence?
- What must be escalated?

## Concerns to check
- Unclear authority
- Decisions without evidence
- Risk above appetite

## Evidence this lens needs
- RACI
- Risk register
- Decision record

## In this act, look for
- 8.1.1.1 S4 Name recorder, judge & by-dates: Recorder and judge are different people.
- 8.1.4.1 S4 Continue, change course or stop?: Judge is not the recorder.
- 8.1.4.2 S4 Finance agrees the realised value?: Finance signs the figure.
- 8.2.4.1 S4 Run cycle retrospective: Check DISCOVER's predictions against outcomes.
- 8.2.4.1 S5 Record learnings with owners: Every learning has an owner and an act.
- 8.3.2.1 S4 Fix now, plan, or accept?: Above-appetite risk goes to the risk owner.
- 8.3.2.1 S5 Update register; record accepted debt: Accepted debt has a revisit date.
- 8.4.2.1 S4 Challenge the recommendation: Independent challenge before the board.
- 8.4.2.1 S5 Recommendation holds?: Recommendation consistent with the scores.
- 8.4.3.1 S3 Iterate, scale, modernise, pivot or retire?: Within the board's authority?
- 8.4.3.1 S4 Record decision & rationale: Rationale and owner recorded.
- 8.4.4.1 S2 Re-rank with WSJF & WIP limits: WIP limit respected.
- 8.4.4.1 S5 Every follow-up acknowledged?: Every receiver acknowledges.
- 8.5.1.1 S1 Confirm scope from the decision: Scope matches the decision.
- 8.5.1.1 S5 Approved by service owner, data owner & sponsor?: Service owner, data owner and sponsor approve.
- 8.5.3.1 S5 Every class verified by a second person?: A second person verifies every class.
- 8.5.4.1 S2 Quiet for the whole period?: Quiet for the whole period before switching off.
- 8.5.4.1 S5 Update inventory; record savings & lessons: Inventory shows Retired.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Workflow 8.1.1.1 · Define the Outcome Measures
files.body:
---
description: "Workflow — Define the Outcome Measures"
argument-hint: <initiative> [extra context]
---

Follow AGENTS.md. Log what you do in PROGRESS.md and register new IDs in TRACE.md.
Load these skills if you can: benefits-realisation-management, goal-question-metric, leading-and-lagging-indicators, heart-framework, comparison-group, outcome-review.
Run it as specified in `workflows/evolve-8-1-1-1-define-measures.md`, stopping at every checkpoint.
Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the product manager on {{initiative}}. I'm working on workflow 8.1.1.1: Define the Outcome Measures.
Goal: Turn every success criterion and the value hypothesis from the brief into a defined metric with baseline source, target, by-date, recorder and judge.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Opportunity brief
- Discovery decision record
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Change released or release date known

## What to do
Work through these steps in order. Show me the output of each step and wait for my OK before the next.
- S1. Extract criteria & value hypothesis (Product manager) → Success criteria & metrics
- S2. Define each metric (Data analyst) → Metric definitions  [if: Nothing measurable → back to DISCOVER]
- S3. Add leading indicators & guardrails (Product manager) → Outcome measurement plan
- S4. Name recorder, judge & by-dates (Product manager) → Outcome measurement plan
- S5. ◆ DECISION — Sponsor agrees the plan? (Sponsor)  [if: Definition disputed → redefine; Target change requested → portfolio board]
At each ◆ decision, prepare the options and a recommendation — I decide.
Cases to handle: Brief gives a value range only; Criterion has no data source yet.
If it fails: Restore the brief's criteria and add the easier metric as a leading indicator; Add a guardrail before the first reading.

## Apply
- Measure what was promised — Judge a change against the success criteria and value hypothesis it was funded on — not against whatever metric looks best now.
- Benefits realisation management — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.
- OKR tracker — Where objectives and key results are published and progress tracked.
- Goal–Question–Metric — Derives metrics top-down: state the goal, ask the questions that show whether it is met, then choose the metrics that answer them.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (quality in use) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Leading & lagging indicators — Pairs lagging outcome measures (the result) with leading indicators that move earlier and predict it, plus guardrails that must not get worse.
- HEART framework — Google's framework for user-centred metrics: Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention and Task success, each traced from goals to signals to metrics.
- Comparison group — Reads an outcome against a comparable group that did not get the change (or got it later) to separate the change's effect from seasonality and other causes.
- Separate recording from judging — Whoever records the readings does not judge them, so numbers are not shaped to a conclusion.
- Outcome dashboard — A live view of each success criterion against its baseline and target, by segment, with the data source behind each tile.
- Outcome review — A scheduled review at the by-date the success criteria set, where readings are compared with targets and the owner decides to continue, change course or stop — and records it.

## Keep in mind
- Business / Strategy: Start from the value hypothesis the brief was funded on.
- Product: Every success criterion carried over verbatim.
- Data: Each metric computable from a named source.
- UX / CX: A task-success or trust measure for the clerks.
- Finance / Commercial: Value expressed in money, agreed with finance.
- Governance / Risk: Recorder and judge are different people.
- Business / Strategy: Sponsor agrees the measures before the numbers arrive.

## Rules
- Rework: Disputed definition → redefine with the analyst

## If it goes off the happy path
- Agreed → confirm baselines
- Disputed definition → redefine
- Target change requested → portfolio board
- Nothing measurable → back to DISCOVER

## Output
- Outcome measurement plan — a table with columns: SC | Metric (definition) | Direction | Baseline | Target | By | Source | Segment | Recorder | Judge | Kind
    (example row: SC-1 | Median order-handling time per order, email received → order in ERP | decrease | 14 min | 8 min | 2026-01-31 | ERP timestamps + mailbox log | Per site | Data analyst | Product manager | Outcome)

## Before you finish, check
- [ ] Every brief criterion present
- [ ] Recorder ≠ judge
- [ ] Plan agreed by the sponsor

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

Run this subprocess end to end with me, one workflow at a time, in this order:
- 8.1.1.1 Define the Outcome Measures — gate: Measurement plan agreed
    produces: Outcome measurement plan
- In parallel: Metric definitions ∥ source checks with the data analyst
After each workflow, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate workflow prompts if we need more depth.

- Leading & lagging indicators — Pairs lagging outcome measures (the result) with leading indicators that move earlier and predict it, plus guardrails that must not get worse.
- Outcome review — A scheduled review at the by-date the success criteria set, where readings are compared with targets and the owner decides to continue, change course or stop — and records it.
- Measure what was promised — Judge a change against the success criteria and value hypothesis it was funded on — not against whatever metric looks best now.
- Separate recording from judging — Whoever records the readings does not judge them, so numbers are not shaped to a conclusion.
- Goal–Question–Metric — Derives metrics top-down: state the goal, ask the questions that show whether it is met, then choose the metrics that answer them.
- Comparison group — Reads an outcome against a comparable group that did not get the change (or got it later) to separate the change's effect from seasonality and other causes.

- Product (required)
- Business / Strategy (required)
- Data (required)
- Concern: Vanity metrics
- Concern: Moving goalposts
- Constraint: Targets are fixed by the brief

- Targets from the brief are not changed in EVOLVE — a change goes to the portfolio board
- Outcome measures are set before release wherever possible

- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Definition disputed → redefine with the data analyst
- A different valid path appears → Small change → reuse the product's standing metrics
- It goes beyond my authority → Sponsor wants new targets → portfolio board
- It should stop → No measurable criterion can be defined → stop measuring and raise it to DISCOVER — recorded in the learning log

- Outcome measurement plan — a table with columns: SC | Metric (definition) | Direction | Baseline | Target | By | Source | Segment | Recorder | Judge | Kind

## What to do
Work through these steps in order. Show me the output of each step and wait for my OK before the next.
- S1. Locate or reconstruct baselines (Data analyst) → Baseline record  [if: No baseline possible → 'cannot tell']
- S2. Check event capture & completeness (Data analyst) → Instrumentation check
- S3. Reconcile with an independent count (Data analyst) → Instrumentation check
- S4. ◆ DECISION — Fit for judging? (Data analyst)  [if: Not fit → fix instrumentation and re-check; Fix needs unplanned work → product owner]

At each ◆ decision, prepare the options and a recommendation — I decide.
Cases to handle: No pre-change data; Definition drifted since the baseline.
If it fails: Re-compute both baseline and readings on one definition; Use the not-yet-live site as a comparison group.

## Apply
- Benefits realisation management — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.
- Comparison group — Reads an outcome against a comparable group that did not get the change (or got it later) to separate the change's effect from seasonality and other causes.
- Analytics — Measures real behaviour — visits, clicks, sign-ups, usage — for experiments and baselines.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (measurability of quality in use) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Pre-registered experiments — The hypothesis, metric and success threshold are written down before the experiment runs, so results can't be reinterpreted afterwards.
- Goal–Question–Metric — Derives metrics top-down: state the goal, ask the questions that show whether it is met, then choose the metrics that answer them.
- Separate recording from judging — Whoever records the readings does not judge them, so numbers are not shaped to a conclusion.
- Leading & lagging indicators — Pairs lagging outcome measures (the result) with leading indicators that move earlier and predict it, plus guardrails that must not get worse.
- Prefer ranges to false precision — Express estimates as ranges with confidence, not single numbers.
- Outcome dashboard — A live view of each success criterion against its baseline and target, by segment, with the data source behind each tile.

## Keep in mind
- Data: Baseline uses the same definition as the plan.
- Engineering: Events fire on every path, including manual fallbacks.
- Privacy: No personal data in event payloads beyond need.
- Quality / Testing: Reconcile against an independent manual sample.
- Data: Not fit for judging means not judged.
- Product: Caveats visible to whoever reads the dashboard.

## Rules
- Rework: Not fit → fix instrumentation and re-check

## If it goes off the happy path
- Fit → record
- Not fit → fix and re-check
- Fix needs unplanned work → product owner
- No baseline → 'cannot tell'

## Output
- Baseline record — a table with columns: SC | Baseline value | Period | Sample size | Method | Confidence | Notes
    (example row: SC-1 | 14.0 min (median) | 2025-03-03 → 2025-03-14 | 1,140 | ERP timestamps vs mailbox receipt | High | Same inbox sample as DISCOVER (PS-01))
- Instrumentation check — fill these fields: Metric (SC); Event / field captured; Completeness; Reconciled against; Defects found; Fix and backlog item; Result (Fit for judging / Fit with caveat / Not fit); Checked by; Date

## Apply
- Benefits realisation management — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.

- Outcome review — A scheduled review at the by-date the success criteria set, where readings are compared with targets and the owner decides to continue, change course or stop — and records it.
- Retrospective — A structured, blameless look back at a piece of work to decide what to keep, stop and change — held for every outcome, including kills.
- Measure what was promised — Judge a change against the success criteria and value hypothesis it was funded on — not against whatever metric looks best now.
- Separate recording from judging — Whoever records the readings does not judge them, so numbers are not shaped to a conclusion.
- Decide explicitly — Every gate ends in a named decision with an owner and a rationale — never by default.
- Goal–Question–Metric — Derives metrics top-down: state the goal, ask the questions that show whether it is met, then choose the metrics that answer them.

## Apply
- Benefits realisation management — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.
- HEART framework — Google's framework for user-centred metrics: Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention and Task success, each traced from goals to signals to metrics.

- Goal–Question–Metric — Derives metrics top-down: state the goal, ask the questions that show whether it is met, then choose the metrics that answer them.
- Comparison group — Reads an outcome against a comparable group that did not get the change (or got it later) to separate the change's effect from seasonality and other causes.

- Affinity clustering — Groups individual observations into themes from the bottom up, letting patterns emerge from the data.

- Privacy: Personal details removed before publishing.

- Product withdrawn → stop

    - Implication: What it suggests we do — not yet a solution.

    - Discarded: Patterns that did not hold up, and why.

Run this process end to end with me, one subprocess at a time, in this order:
- 8.3.1 Identify & Record Debt — gate: Debt Recorded
    produces: Tech-debt register
- 8.3.2 Assess Interest & Risk — gate: Debt Ranked
    produces: Debt interest assessment, Tech-debt register
- 8.3.3 Plan Paydown & Modernisation — gate: Modernisation Plan Approved

## Apply
- DORA metrics — The DevOps Research and Assessment measures of software delivery performance: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service (with reliability).
- SRE — Site Reliability Engineering: runs services with explicit service-level objectives and error budgets, and treats toil and reliability work as engineering to be reduced.
- ISO/IEC 14764 (maintenance types) — ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022 Software engineering — Software life cycle processes — Maintenance.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (maintainability) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Strangler fig — Replaces a legacy component gradually: new code grows around the old behind the same interface, traffic moves over slice by slice, and the old part is removed when nothing uses it.
- Parallel run — Runs the old and the new implementation side by side on the same inputs and compares outputs before switching over.
- Fitness functions — Automated checks that measure an architectural characteristic — such as coupling, latency or use of a deprecated API — so modernisation progress and erosion are visible.

- Make debt visible — Technical debt is managed only when it is written down, quantified and ranked alongside features.

- Engineering (required)
- Architecture (required)
- Product (required)

- S2. Add debt, run cost & capacity (Engineering lead)

- Portfolio register — The list of initiatives with sponsor, stage, status and investment.
- Decision record — A short, versioned record of a significant decision: its context, the options, the choice and its consequences.
- Weighted scoring — Scores options against weighted criteria so trade-offs are explicit and comparable.
- No surprises for decision-makers — Decision-makers hear bad news early and directly, never for the first time at the gate.
- ISO 31000 (recording & reporting) — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- Portfolio review — A quarterly review where the portfolio board looks at each initiative's outcomes, costs and risks and decides to iterate, scale, modernise, pivot or retire, then re-ranks the backlog.
- Lean Portfolio Management — Manages a portfolio of initiatives as flow: strategy and investment funding, lean governance and participatory budgeting, with work limited and ranked by economics.

## What to do
Work through these steps in order. Show me the output of each step and wait for my OK before the next.
- S1. Describe the five options (Product manager) → Options appraisal  [if: Nothing left worth doing → recommend close]
- S2. Estimate value, cost & risk (Finance partner) → Portfolio options appraisal

Cases to handle: Combination scores best; Retire close to continue.

## Apply
- 7 Rs of modernisation — A menu of options for each component: retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, re-architect, replace (repurchase).
- Retire on purpose — Things are switched off deliberately — with users moved, data handled and costs removed — not left to decay.
- Lean Portfolio Management — Manages a portfolio of initiatives as flow: strategy and investment funding, lean governance and participatory budgeting, with work limited and ranked by economics.
- Spreadsheet model — A transparent model where assumptions, formulas and ranges are visible and adjustable.
- Four big risks — Every product idea carries four risks; good discovery addresses all four before building.
- Cost of delay — Estimates the value lost per unit of time by not delivering, to compare urgency.
- Weighted scoring — Scores options against weighted criteria so trade-offs are explicit and comparable.
- WSJF — Weighted Shortest Job First: rank work by cost of delay divided by job size, so the most valuable small items go first.
- Scoring model — A shared sheet with criteria, weights and scores so ratings are consistent.
- Scoring workshop — Stakeholders score options together against agreed criteria, discussing the evidence behind each score.
- Pre-mortem — Imagine the initiative failed; list the reasons; turn the likeliest into mitigations.
- Sunk cost is not a reason — Past spend does not justify future spend; decide on the value still to come.
- ISO 31000 (risk treatment options) — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- Kill early, kill cheaply — Stopping a weak idea early is a success, not a failure.
- Decision record — A short, versioned record of a significant decision: its context, the options, the choice and its consequences.

- Business / Strategy: Iterate, scale, modernise, pivot and retire all written down.
- Customer / User: What each option means for users.
- Finance / Commercial: Value and cost as ranges.
- Architecture: Modernise option sized by the architect.
- Vendor / Third Party: Vendor terms behind each option.
- Product: Scores cite evidence.
- Governance / Risk: Independent challenge before the board.
- Legal: Contract and exit obligations per option.
- Governance / Risk: Recommendation consistent with the scores.

## Rules
- Rework: Challenge succeeds → re-estimate and re-score

## If it goes off the happy path
- Holds → decide
- Challenge succeeds → re-estimate
- Cross-initiative → board chair
- Nothing left → recommend close

- Portfolio options appraisal — a table with columns: Option | What it means here | Value (€/yr) | Cost | Risk | Cost of delay | Evidence | Score

## What to do

- 8.4.2 Evaluate Options — gate: Options Assessed

- Dependency mapping — Lists everything that depends on an item — users, systems, reports, contracts and data flows — before changing or retiring it.

files.body:
---
description: "Process — Retirement & Decommission"
argument-hint: <initiative> [extra context]
---

Follow AGENTS.md. Log what you do in PROGRESS.md and register new IDs in TRACE.md.
Load these skills if you can: 7-rs-of-modernisation, dependency-mapping, stakeholder-interviews, deprecation-window, pre-mortem, closing-the-feedback-loop, itil-4, kanban (+5 more).
Run it as specified in `workflows/evolve-8-5-retire.md`, stopping at every checkpoint.
Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the service owner on {{initiative}}. I'm working on process 8.5: Retirement & Decommission.
Goal: Retire products, features, components and tools deliberately, so users are moved, data is handled lawfully and cost and risk really go away.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Portfolio decision record
- Service inventory
- Retention schedule
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Portfolio decision to retire, or a retire slice of a modernisation
- Replacement path available

## What to do
Run this process end to end with me, one subprocess at a time, in this order:
- 8.5.1 Plan the Retirement — gate: Retirement Plan Approved
    produces: Retirement plan
- 8.5.2 Notify & Transition Users — gate: Users Transitioned
    produces: Sunset notice, Transition tracker
- 8.5.3 Retain, Migrate or Dispose of Data — gate: Data Disposition Approved
    produces: Data disposition record, Deletion certificate
- 8.5.4 Decommission & Close — gate: Decommission Sign-off
    produces: Decommission record, Learning log
- In parallel: Notice ∥ contract terminations
- In parallel: Migration ∥ archiving
After each subprocess, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate subprocess prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Decommission Sign-off review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 (service retirement) — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 (disposal process) — ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017 Systems and software engineering — Software life cycle processes.
- ISO 15489 — ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management.
- GDPR (storage limitation & erasure) — Regulation (EU) 2016/679, the General Data Protection Regulation.
- ISO/IEC 27001 (information deletion) — ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems — Requirements.
- Deprecation window — Announces a retirement with a fixed notice period, a read-only or warning phase and a published switch-off date, so consumers can move in time.
- Parallel run — Runs the old and the new implementation side by side on the same inputs and compares outputs before switching over.
- Data migration reconciliation — Proves a migration moved data completely and correctly by reconciling counts, totals and samples between source and target before the source is disposed of.
- Retire on purpose — Things are switched off deliberately — with users moved, data handled and costs removed — not left to decay.
- Keep only the data you must — When something retires, keep exactly what the law or the business requires, for as long as required, and delete the rest.

## Keep in mind
- Operations (required)
- Data (required)
- Privacy (required)
- Customer / User (required)
- Governance / Risk (required)
- Concern: Hidden dependants
- Concern: Unlawful retention or deletion
- Concern: Zombie systems
- Constraint: Retention schedule
- Constraint: Notice periods
- Constraint: Legal holds

## Rules
- Read-only before off; off before removal
- Never delete records under retention or legal hold
- Credentials revoked on switch-off day
- Change management policy
- Records retention schedule
- Privacy policy

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Dependant without a path or reconciliation failure → re-plan / re-migrate
- A different valid path appears → Partial retirement → feature removed through PLAN
- It goes beyond my authority → Legal hold, date change or shared platform → legal / sponsor / platform owner
- It should stop → Replacement cannot serve users → retirement stopped; back to 8.4 — recorded in the learning log

## Output
- Retirement plan — a document with these sections:
    - 1. What retires and why: Scope and the decision behind it.
    - 2. Who and what is affected: Users, dependent systems, contracts, data — from the service inventory.
    - 3. Replacement path: Where users and consumers go instead.
    - 4. Data disposition: Keep, migrate, archive or delete — per class, with the retention rule.
    - 5. Timeline: Notice, read-only period, switch-off, removal.
    - 6. Proof of switch-off: How we will know it is really gone.
- Sunset notice — a message to All order clerks; Ops managers Sites A–C; Support; BI team: a subject line and a short body
- Transition tracker — a table with columns: Group / consumer | Count | Notified | Moved to | Moved | Blocker | Owner
    (example row: Clerks Rotterdam | 14 | 2026-03-02 | Auto-fill review screen | 100% | — | Ops manager A)
- Data disposition record — a table with columns: Data class | Where held | Personal data? | Rule (retention schedule) | Disposition | Destination | Done | Verified by
    (example row: Customer codes | Clerks' sheets | ☐ | Business data — keep while customer active | Migrate | ERP customer master | 2026-03-27 | Data owner)
- Deletion certificate — fill these fields: Retirement; Data class; Locations covered; Action (Securely deleted / Archived / Migrated); Method; Backups; Performed by; Verified by; Date; Signature
- Decommission record — a document with these sections:
    - Switch-off: Read-only period, scream-test result and the final switch-off.
    - Removed: Infra, jobs, accounts, credentials, DNS, mailbox rules, monitoring, licences.
    - Data: Link to the data disposition record and certificates.
    - Inventory: Service inventory / CMDB updated.
    - Savings: Run cost and risk removed.
    - Lessons: What to do differently — copied to the learning log.

## Before you finish, check
- [ ] Every dependant moved
- [ ] Every data class disposed per rule and verified
- [ ] Zero use after switch-off
- [ ] No use after switch-off
- [ ] Data disposed per the retention schedule and certified
- [ ] Inventory shows Retired
- [ ] Savings and lessons recorded

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## What to do
Run this act end to end with me, one process at a time, in this order:
- 8.1 Outcome Measurement — gate: Outcome Review
    produces: Outcome measurement plan, Baseline record, Outcome readings log, Outcome report, Realised value reconciliation
- 8.2 Feedback & Insight Synthesis — gate: Insight Review

At the end, prepare the Portfolio Decision review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- Benefits realisation management — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.
- ITIL 4 — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- Lean Portfolio Management — Manages a portfolio of initiatives as flow: strategy and investment funding, lean governance and participatory budgeting, with work limited and ranked by economics.
- DORA metrics — The DevOps Research and Assessment measures of software delivery performance: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service (with reliability).
- ISO 31000 (monitoring & review) — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- ISO/IEC 14764 — ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022 Software engineering — Software life cycle processes — Maintenance.
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 (disposal process) — ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017 Systems and software engineering — Software life cycle processes.
- ISO 15489 — ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management.
- GDPR (storage limitation) — Regulation (EU) 2016/679, the General Data Protection Regulation.
- Leading & lagging indicators — Pairs lagging outcome measures (the result) with leading indicators that move earlier and predict it, plus guardrails that must not get worse.

## Keep in mind
- Business / Strategy (required)
- Product (required)
- Customer / User (required)
- Data (required)
- Concern: Measuring output instead of outcome
- Concern: Learning that never reaches a backlog
- Concern: Zombie systems and hidden debt
- Constraint: Targets fixed by the brief

- Constraint: Retention law

## Rules

## If it goes off the happy path

- It should stop → Retire → 8.5, ending in a decommission record; stopping pursuit of an outcome is a recorded decision — both in the learning log

## Output
- Outcome report — a document with these sections:
    - 1. What we promised: The value hypothesis and success criteria from the opportunity brief, verbatim.
    - 2. What we measured: Each criterion: baseline, target, latest reading, met / not met / cannot tell.
    - 3. Value realised: Run-rate value against the hypothesis, reconciled with finance.
    - 4. Why: What explains the gap — linked insights and confounders.
    - 5. Decision: Continue, change course or stop — with the reason and the next reading date.
    - 6. Follow-ups: Improvement items, debt items and opportunities raised.
- Insight synthesis — a document with these sections:
    - Insight INS-##: We observed … because … so we believe … (confidence: high / medium / low).
    - Evidence: The signals behind it — at least two independent kinds.
    - Implication: What it suggests we do — not yet a solution.
    - Other insights: One block per insight.
    - Discarded: Patterns that did not hold up, and why.
- Improvement backlog — a table with columns: IMP | Improvement | From | Size | Route | Linked item | Owner | Status
    (example row: IMP-021 | Match PDF customer numbers to the ERP customer master automatically | INS-12, OUT-004 | S | PLAN (product backlog) | FEA-044 | Product owner | Routed)
- Tech-debt register — a table with columns: TDR | Debt | Quadrant | Found from | Interest (per quarter) | Risk / deadline | Cost to fix | Rank | Plan | Status
    (example row: TDR-007 | One hand-written parsing template per customer PDF layout, held in config | Deliberate–prudent | Sprint 9 retro | ~1.5 dev-days per new layout; 6 layouts a quarter | None | M | 2 | MOD-03 | Planned)
- Modernisation plan — a document with these sections:
    - 1. What and why: The debt items it pays and the risk or interest it removes.
    - 2. Approach: Which of the 7 Rs, and the pattern used.
    - 3. Slices and sequence: Small, independently releasable steps.
    - 4. Capacity and cost: How much of the team, for how long; in flow or as a funded item.
    - 5. Risks and rollback: What could go wrong and how to go back.
    - 6. Done when: Measurable exit criteria and fitness functions.
- Portfolio decision record — a document with these sections:
    - Context: What was decided and on what evidence.
    - Options considered: From the options appraisal, including retire.
    - Decision: One or more of iterate / scale / modernise / pivot / retire.
    - Rationale: Why, citing the pack.
    - Conditions and funding: What must hold; capacity or money released.
    - Routing: Where each piece of work goes now.
    - Next review: Date or measurable trigger for the next portfolio review.
- Retirement plan — a document with these sections:
    - 1. What retires and why: Scope and the decision behind it.
    - 2. Who and what is affected: Users, dependent systems, contracts, data — from the service inventory.
    - 3. Replacement path: Where users and consumers go instead.
    - 4. Data disposition: Keep, migrate, archive or delete — per class, with the retention rule.
    - 5. Timeline: Notice, read-only period, switch-off, removal.
    - 6. Proof of switch-off: How we will know it is really gone.
- Decommission record — a document with these sections:
    - Switch-off: Read-only period, scream-test result and the final switch-off.
    - Removed: Infra, jobs, accounts, credentials, DNS, mailbox rules, monitoring, licences.
    - Data: Link to the data disposition record and certificates.
    - Inventory: Service inventory / CMDB updated.
    - Savings: Run cost and risk removed.
    - Lessons: What to do differently — copied to the learning log.
- Opportunity signal / request — fill these fields: What did you notice or want?; Who is affected?; What happens today?; Why now?; Raised by; Date raised; Channel (Form / Email / Meeting / Support ticket / Other)
- Product backlog — a table with columns: ID | Type | Title | Parent | Outcome it serves | Evidence | Estimate | Order | Status

# Guardrails & hooks — Evolve

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Solo / small
- Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.
- Watch for: Skipping discovery because 'I already know'
- Watch for: Accepting agent output unreviewed because there's no one else to check it

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |

| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |

files.title: How to use this kit
files.body:
# Node agent kit — Evolve

A ready project folder for running this act with your agent. People drive, decide and sign off; agents help.

## What's inside
- **Context file** — `AGENTS.md`: What the agent always knows about the initiative: how we work, the lifecycle, conventions, trace IDs, templates, ground rules and scale.
- **Skills** — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: Reusable how-to packages — one per technique or method — with steps, structure, output templates and checks. The agent loads one when the task needs it.
- **Commands** — `commands/<name>.md`: Saved prompts you run by name, with arguments — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act.
- **Workflows** — `workflows/<name>.md`: A run specification: steps in order, inputs and outputs as files, who owns each step, human checkpoints, decision branches, recovery and the gate.
- **Subagents** — `agents/<name>.md`: Specialised helpers with one job — lens reviewers (privacy, security, finance…), a researcher, a synthesiser, a challenger, a decision-brief writer.
- **Tools & connectors** — `TOOLS.md`: Which tools and data each step needs — web search, documents, spreadsheets, the backlog tool, the research repository, the code repository — and what each scale allows the agent to do with them.
- **Guardrails & hooks** — `GUARDRAILS.md`: Rules the agent must follow and automatic checks at key moments — before saving an artifact, before a decision, before sending anything outside the team.
- **Rubrics** — `rubrics/<artifact>.md`: A scored checklist for each artifact, from its template, quality criteria and the unit's criteria.
- **Memory & handoff** — `PROGRESS.md · TRACE.md · docs/`: What carries across sessions and people: the project folder, a progress log, and a trace-ID register.
- **Templates** — `templates/`: the artifact templates the work produces.

## Set it up
1. Put this folder at the root of your project repository or shared drive and fill `{{initiative}}` in AGENTS.md.
2. Point your agent at it — how each layer is picked up:
   - Context file: Many coding agents read AGENTS.md at the repository root. Tools with their own file (e.g. CLAUDE.md) can import or copy it. In chat assistants, paste it into the project's instructions.
   - Skills: Agents that support skills load SKILL.md folders from their skills directory. Otherwise attach the SKILL.md as a file, or paste it before the prompt.
   - Commands: Agents with custom commands or saved prompts read Markdown files from their commands / prompts folder; $ARGUMENTS takes what you type after the name. Otherwise paste the file.
   - Workflows: Point the agent at the workflow file ("run workflows/x.md, stop at every checkpoint"). Orchestration tools can execute the YAML block; people can read it as a checklist.
   - Subagents: Agents that support subagents load them from their agents folder. Otherwise open a separate conversation and paste the file as its first message.
   - Tools & connectors: Connect tools through your agent's connectors or MCP servers; grant the least access the step needs.
   - Guardrails & hooks: Agents with hooks can run these checks automatically; everywhere else they're a checklist the agent applies and you confirm.
   - Rubrics: Any agent: "score docs/x.md against rubrics/x.md".
   - Memory & handoff: Keep them in the repository or shared drive the agent can read; start each session with "read PROGRESS.md".
3. Start with the command `evolve-run-act`, or the command for the unit you're on.
4. After every step: check the output, score it against its rubric, save it in `docs/`, and log it in PROGRESS.md.

Tools change quickly — check your agent's documentation for where it reads context files, skills, commands and subagents.

files.body:
---
name: 7-rs-of-modernisation
description: "A menu of options for each component: retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, re-architect, replace (repurchase). Use when choosing a modernisation approach. In Node: 8.3.3.1 S2 Choose approach (7 Rs); 8.4.2.1 S1 Describe the five options; 8.5.1.1 S1 Confirm scope from the decision."
---

# 7 Rs of modernisation

_Method_ — A menu of options for each component: retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, re-architect, replace (repurchase).

## When to use it
Choosing a modernisation approach.

Applied in Node at:
- 8.3.3.1 S2 Choose approach (7 Rs) — command `evolve-8-3-3-1-s2-choose-approach-7-rs`
- 8.4.2.1 S1 Describe the five options — command `evolve-8-4-2-1-s1-describe-the-five-options`
- 8.5.1.1 S1 Confirm scope from the decision — command `evolve-8-5-1-1-s1-confirm-scope-from-the-decision`

## How to do it
1. Inventory the components
2. Choose one R per component, with a reason
3. Sequence by risk and value
4. Record the choice in the modernisation plan

## Structure
| R | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Retain | Keep as is, for now |
| Retire | Switch off |
| Rehost | Move as is |
| Replatform | Move with small changes (e.g. new API version) |
| Refactor | Restructure code, same behaviour |
| Re-architect | Change the structure substantially |
| Replace | Buy or adopt something else |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Modernisation plan → `templates/modernisation-plan.md`, saved as `docs/modernisation-plan.md`
- Options appraisal → `templates/options-appraisal.md`, saved as `docs/options-appraisal.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Re-architecting by default
- Modernisation plan: Names the debt it pays
- Modernisation plan: Sliced into releasable steps
- Modernisation plan: Exit criteria measurable
- Options appraisal: Retire is always considered
- Options appraisal: Every option cites evidence
- Options appraisal: Scores use the agreed scoring model
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Gartner 5 Rs; AWS 7 Rs

# Benefits realisation management

_Framework_ — Plans, tracks and confirms the benefits an investment was made for, from the business case through to after delivery, so value is realised rather than assumed.

## When to use it
Every initiative with a value hypothesis — measured after release, not just at the business case.

---

description: "A human-centred problem-solving framework that alternates between understanding people and testing ideas with them, so solutions are anchored in real needs. Use when when the problem is ambiguous or human behaviour drives success. In Node: 8.2.2.1 S3 Trace causes & write insights."
---

# Design Thinking

_Framework_ — A human-centred problem-solving framework that alternates between understanding people and testing ideas with them, so solutions are anchored in real needs.

## When to use it
When the problem is ambiguous or human behaviour drives success.

Applied in Node at:
- 8.2.2.1 S3 Trace causes & write insights (applied as: define) — command `evolve-8-2-2-1-s3-trace-causes-and-write-insights`

## How to do it
1. Empathise — observe and interview the people affected
2. Define — turn what you learned into a sharp, human problem statement
3. Ideate — generate many possible directions
4. Prototype — make cheap, tangible versions of the best ideas
5. Test — put prototypes in front of users and learn; loop back as needed

## Structure
1. **Empathise** — Who are they, what do they do, feel and need?
2. **Define** — What is the real problem, in their terms?
3. **Ideate** — How might we…? Go wide before narrowing.
4. **Prototype** — What is the cheapest thing that answers our question?
5. **Test** — What did users actually do? What changes?
→ then repeat

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Insight statements → `templates/insight-synthesis.md`, saved as `docs/insight-synthesis.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Jumping to Ideate without real empathy work
- Avoid: Treating it as a linear checklist instead of a loop
- Insight statements: Each insight cites two or more independent signals
- Insight statements: Confidence stated
- Insight statements: No solution words in the insight
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

---

# ITIL 4

_Framework_ — AXELOS's framework for IT service management. Its service value system links demand to value through governance, practices and continual improvement, and covers services from design to retirement.

## When to use it
Continual improvement of running services, service portfolio decisions and service retirement.

Applied in Node at:
- 8.1.4.1 S5 Record & sign the outcome report (applied as: continual improvement model) — command `evolve-8-1-4-1-s4-record-and-sign-the-outcome-report`
- 8.2.1.1 S1 List channels & owners (applied as: service value chain: engage) — command `evolve-8-2-1-1-s1-list-channels-and-owners`
- 8.2.3.1 S1 Write improvement items (applied as: continual improvement register) — command `evolve-8-2-3-1-s1-write-improvement-items`
- 8.2.4.1 S5 Record learnings with owners (applied as: continual improvement) — command `evolve-8-2-4-1-s4-record-learnings-with-owners`
- 8.3.3.1 S5 Approve in flow, or needs funding? (applied as: continual improvement) — command `evolve-8-3-3-1-d1-approve-in-flow-or-needs-funding`
- 8.5.2.1 S3 End contracts & licences (applied as: service retirement) — command `evolve-8-5-2-1-s3-end-contracts-and-licences`
- 8.5.3.1 S3 Archive records under retention (applied as: information and data management) — command `evolve-8-5-3-1-s3-archive-records-under-retention`
- 8.5.4.1 S5 Update inventory; record savings & lessons (applied as: service configuration management) — command `evolve-8-5-4-1-s4-update-inventory-record-savings-and-lessons`

## How to do it
1. Start from the value the service co-creates with its consumers
2. Run the service value chain: plan, improve, engage, design & transition, obtain / build, deliver & support
3. Apply the continual improvement model to every service
4. Retire services deliberately through service configuration and portfolio management

## Structure
1. **What is the vision?** — Business goals
2. **Where are we now?** — Baseline assessment
3. **Where do we want to be?** — Measurable targets
4. **How do we get there?** — Improvement plan
5. **Take action** — Execute the plan
6. **Did we get there?** — Measurements and KPIs
7. **How do we keep the momentum going?** — Embed and repeat
→ then repeat

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Outcome report vs hypothesis → `templates/outcome-report.md`, saved as `docs/outcome-report.md`
- Improvement item → `templates/improvement-backlog.md`, saved as `docs/improvement-backlog.md`
- Learning log → `templates/learning-log.md`, saved as `docs/learning-log.md`
- Archive verification → `templates/deletion-certificate.md`, saved as `docs/deletion-certificate.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Adopting every practice as a heavy process
- Avoid: Improvement registers no one prioritises
- Outcome report vs hypothesis: Every criterion from the brief is reported
- Outcome report vs hypothesis: Gap explained with evidence, not opinion
- Outcome report vs hypothesis: Decision explicit and dated
- Improvement item: Every item names its source insight or gap
- Improvement item: Every item routed or dropped with a reason
- Improvement item: Small items go to PLAN, new opportunities to DISCOVER
- Learning log: Every stop and decision has an entry
- Learning log: Each learning names a change and an owner
- Archive verification: Backups and copies covered
- Archive verification: Performer and verifier differ
- Decommission record: No traffic or use after switch-off
- Decommission record: Inventory updated
- Decommission record: Savings stated
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

AXELOS, ITIL 4 Foundation (2019)

# Multi-level backlog

_Pattern_ — Keeps work in linked backlogs at different sizes and horizons — initiatives, epics and features, stories — each owned and refined at its own cadence, so strategy traces down to the sprint and evidence traces back up.

## When to use it
Any organisation running more than one team or initiative.

# Retrospective

_Practice_ — A structured, blameless look back at a piece of work to decide what to keep, stop and change — held for every outcome, including kills.

## When to use it
At the end of discovery, whatever the decision, and after any stop.

3. Score each option 1–5
4. Multiply and sum

## Structure
| Criterion | Weight | Score (1–5) | Weighted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User value | 30% |  |  |
| Business value | 30% |  |  |
| Effort (inverse) | 20% |  |  |
| Risk (inverse) | 20% |  |  |
| Total | 100% |  | Σ |

- Debt ranking → `templates/debt-assessment.md`, saved as `docs/debt-assessment.md`

- Debt ranking: Deadlines drive cost of delay

- Portfolio review pack: Recommendation separate from evidence

files.title: WSJF
files.body:
---
name: wsjf
description: "Weighted Shortest Job First: rank work by cost of delay divided by job size, so the most valuable small items go first. Use when ranking initiatives in the portfolio backlog and large features in the product backlog. In Node: 8.2.3.1 S2 Size each item; 8.3.2.1 S3 Score WSJF against features; 8.4.2.1 S3 Score with the agreed model; 8.4.3.1 S5 Set conditions, funding & next review; 8.4.4.1 S2 Re-rank with WSJF & WIP limits."
---

# WSJF

_Technique_ — Weighted Shortest Job First: rank work by cost of delay divided by job size, so the most valuable small items go first.

## When to use it
Ranking initiatives in the portfolio backlog and large features in the product backlog.

Applied in Node at:
- 8.2.3.1 S2 Size each item — command `evolve-8-2-3-1-s2-size-each-item`
- 8.3.2.1 S3 Score WSJF against features — command `evolve-8-3-2-1-s3-score-wsjf-against-features`
- 8.4.2.1 S3 Score with the agreed model — command `evolve-8-4-2-1-s3-score-with-the-agreed-model`
- 8.4.3.1 S5 Set conditions, funding & next review — command `evolve-8-4-3-1-s4-set-conditions-funding-and-next-review`
- 8.4.4.1 S2 Re-rank with WSJF & WIP limits — command `evolve-8-4-4-1-s2-re-rank-with-wsjf-and-wip-limits`

## How to do it
1. Estimate cost of delay (value + time criticality + risk reduction)
2. Estimate job size
3. Divide and rank

## Structure
> WSJF = cost of delay ÷ job size → highest first.

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Improvement backlog → `templates/improvement-backlog.md`, saved as `docs/improvement-backlog.md`
- Debt ranking → `templates/debt-assessment.md`, saved as `docs/debt-assessment.md`
- Portfolio options appraisal → `templates/options-appraisal.md`, saved as `docs/options-appraisal.md`
- Portfolio decision → `templates/portfolio-decision.md`, saved as `docs/portfolio-decision.md`
- Portfolio backlog → `templates/portfolio-backlog.md`, saved as `docs/portfolio-backlog.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: False precision — use relative scales
- Improvement backlog: Every item names its source insight or gap
- Improvement backlog: Every item routed or dropped with a reason
- Improvement backlog: Small items go to PLAN, new opportunities to DISCOVER
- Debt ranking: Interest quantified, not asserted
- Debt ranking: Deadlines drive cost of delay
- Portfolio options appraisal: Retire is always considered
- Portfolio options appraisal: Every option cites evidence
- Portfolio options appraisal: Scores use the agreed scoring model
- Portfolio decision: Retire considered explicitly
- Portfolio decision: Rationale cites evidence
- Portfolio decision: Routing named for every follow-up
- Portfolio backlog: Every initiative links to its decision record
- Portfolio backlog: Ranked by value, cost of delay and size
- Portfolio backlog: Active initiatives limited
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## 1. What and why

_What could go wrong and how to go back._
> Example: v3 field mapping differs → parallel run compares every order; rollback = flag off.

## Options considered
_From the options appraisal, including retire._
> Example: Scale; Modernise; Iterate; Retire.


## Decision
_One or more of iterate / scale / modernise / pivot / retire._
> Example: Scale to Antwerp with customer-code matching, and Modernise the connector (MOD-03).


## Rationale
_Why, citing the pack._
> Example: Value inside the hypothesis range; gap explained by INS-12, fixable cheaply; API v2 end of support makes modernising time-critical.


## Conditions and funding
_What must hold; capacity or money released._
> Example: Customer-code matching live before Antwerp; 15% capacity for MOD-03; no new funding.


## Routing
_Where each piece of work goes now._
> Example: IMP-021 → PLAN; REQ-031 → DISCOVER; RET-002 (legacy OrderKey macro) → Retirement; INI-004 re-ranked 2nd.


## Next review
_Date or measurable trigger for the next portfolio review._
> Example: Q2 2026 planning, or earlier if SC-1 at Rotterdam rises above 10 min.

- Sponsor: ____________  Date: ______

files.body:
# Workflow 8.1.1.1 · Define the Outcome Measures

Turn every success criterion and the value hypothesis from the brief into a defined metric with baseline source, target, by-date, recorder and judge.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/evolve-8-1-1-1-define-measures.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `evolve-8-1-1-1-run-define-measures`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: evolve-8-1-1-1-define-measures
title: "Define the Outcome Measures"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 8.1.2.1 · Verify Baselines & Instrumentation

Locate each baseline, check the data behind each metric is captured and correct, and fix what is broken before readings count.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/evolve-8-1-2-1-verify-instrumentation.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `evolve-8-1-2-1-run-verify-instrumentation`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: evolve-8-1-2-1-verify-instrumentation
title: "Verify Baselines & Instrumentation"
owner: "Data analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/measurement-plan.md"
  - "docs/operational-signals.md"
preconditions:
  - "Measurement plan agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Locate or reconstruct baselines"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-2-1-s1-locate-or-reconstruct-baselines
    skills: [benefits-realisation-management, comparison-group]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/baseline-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "No baseline possible → 'cannot tell'": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Check event capture & completeness"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-2-1-s2-check-event-capture-and-completeness
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/instrumentation-check.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Reconcile with an independent count"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-2-1-s3-reconcile-with-an-independent-count
    skills: [pre-registered-experiments, goal-question-metric]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/instrumentation-check.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Fit for judging?"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Data analyst decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Not fit → fix instrumentation and re-check": s2
      "Fix needs unplanned work → product owner": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Record fitness & caveats"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-2-1-s4-record-fitness-and-caveats
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/baseline-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Instrumentation verified"
criteria:
  - "Completeness ≥ 98%"
  - "Same definition as the plan"
checks:
  - "Independent count reconciliation"
on_failure:
  - "Re-compute both baseline and readings on one definition"
  - "Use the not-yet-live site as a comparison group"
rework: "Not fit → fix instrumentation and re-check"
outputs:
  - "docs/baseline-record.md"
  - "docs/instrumentation-check.md"
handoff: "Baseline record & instrumentation check → 8.1.3 Record Outcome Readings"
learning:
  - "Instrumentation gaps found after release — learning log, for DESIGN and BUILD"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 8.1.3.1 · Take & Record a Reading Round

On each cadence, read every criterion per segment, check it against the comparison group, and record it append-only for the review.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/evolve-8-1-3-1-readings.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `evolve-8-1-3-1-run-readings`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: evolve-8-1-3-1-readings
title: "Take & Record a Reading Round"
owner: "Data analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/measurement-plan.md"
  - "docs/baseline-record.md"
  - "docs/operational-signals.md"
preconditions:
  - "Instrumentation verified"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Run agreed queries per segment"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-3-1-s1-run-agreed-queries-per-segment
    skills: [goal-question-metric, heart-framework]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/outcome-readings.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Change withdrawn → stop readings": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Compare with comparison group & note caveats"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-3-1-s2-compare-with-comparison-group-and-note-caveats
    skills: [comparison-group, cohort-analysis]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, customer-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/outcome-readings.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Guardrail breached or reading anomalous?"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Data analyst decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Query error → re-run; record a correcting reading": s1
      "Guardrail breach → product manager / sponsor": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Record readings (append-only)"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: evolve-8-1-3-1-s3-record-readings-append-only
    reviewers: [data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/outcome-readings.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish to outcome dashboard"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
```
